Maintenance Report — MNT-0165-004

Asset: WELL-0165 (NE-08 Well 165, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 26 May 2023 08:00 · Finished: 27 May 2023 00:00 · Well stopped for this job: 16 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0165-0032 on 2023-05-25 Report written: 28 May 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0165-0032 at 13:00 on 2023-05-25 found crude oil on the pad: about 1.7% of the pad area, estimated 0.6 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 4.7 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 265 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 212 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.6 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0165-004 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.3% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0165-006

Asset: WELL-0165 (NE-08 Well 165, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 09 Sep 2023 08:00 · Finished: 20 Sep 2023 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 267 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0165-0046 on 2023-09-07 Report written: 20 Sep 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0165-0046 showed the wellhead at 31.1 °C with the air at 29.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0165-0131 showed the wellhead at 27.9 °C with the air at 27.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 8 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

A worn plunger that let sand settle and lock the pump.

  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

  • About 0.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0165-029 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.63% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
